While Bayesian Optimization (BO) provides probabilistically informed candidates, it does not reason about long-term performance trends. To address this limitation, we incorporate a Reinforcement Learning (RL) agent that selects the most promising configuration from each batch of K K candidates proposed by BO. For each candidate x t + 1 ( j ) x_{t+1}^{(j)} , the GP posterior r ​ ( x t + 1 ( j ) ) ∼ 𝒩 ​ ( μ j , σ j 2 ) r(x_{t+1}^{(j)})\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu_{j},\sigma_{j}^{2}) provides predictive statistics. The RL state is the normalized feature vector where min–max normalization is applied across candidates. The agent selects an action a t ∈ { 1 , … , K } a_{t}\in\{1,\dots,K\} using an ϵ \epsilon -greedy rule, to gradually shift from exploration to exploitation. Transitions ( s t , a t , r t , s t + 1 ) (s_{t},a_{t},r_{t},s_{t+1}) are stored in a replay buffer of capacity C C , enabling decorrelated and repeated sampling. The buffer operates as a first-in-first-out (FIFO) queue. The RL agent approximates its action-value function Q ​ ( s , a ) Q(s,a) using a single neural network updated periodically rather than at every step. Every F F iterations ( t mod F = 0 t\bmod F=0 ), a mini-batch of transitions is sampled from the replay buffer, and the network is refined via one-step temporal-difference (TD) learning.
